# The History of Apple Silicon: From A4 to M Series

## Introduction

Apple's journey into custom silicon represents one of the most consequential shifts in the history of personal computing and mobile technology. What began with a single processor designed to power the iPhone in 2010 has grown into a full family of chips spanning smartphones, tablets, laptops, desktops, and media players. This history traces the arc from the humble A4 through the high-performance M4 family, examining how Apple transformed from a consumer of third-party processors into one of the industry's most influential chip designers.

## The A4: The Beginning (2010)

In January 2010, Apple introduced the A4, the first processor designed and manufactured under the Apple brand. Fabricated by Samsung on a 45-nanometer process, the A4 was a system-on-chip combining a single-core ARM Cortex-A8 CPU clocked at 1 GHz with a PowerVR SGX535 GPU

# The History of Apple Silicon: From A4 to M Series

## Introduction

Apple's journey into custom silicon represents one of the most consequential shifts in the history of personal computing and mobile technology. What began with a single processor designed to power the iPhone in 2010 has grown into a full family of chips spanning smartphones, tablets, laptops, desktops, and media players. This history traces the arc from the humble A4 through the high-performance M4 family, examining how Apple transformed from a consumer of third-party processors into one of the industry's most influential chip designers.

## The A4: The Beginning (2010)

In January 2010, Apple introduced the A4, the first processor designed and manufactured under the Apple brand. Fabricated by Samsung on a 45-nanometer process, the A4 was a system-on-chip combining a single-core ARM Cortex-A8 CPU clocked at 1 GHz with a PowerVR SGX535 GPU
